main_text.p: In hoc autem Christi ad- {brace} Mortui. {brace} Viui. uenru congregandi sunt De congregand. ad indic. cap.2.
Mortui sunt, qui ad tubam prædictam, nunquam dissoluedi cum proprijs corporibus resurgent.Dan. 12.1.2.3.Ioa.5.27.28.29.
Viui sunt,qui tunc temporis viuentes ἐν ἀτόμῳ ἐν ῥιπῇ ὀφθαλμοῦ mutabuntur. 1.Cor.15.52.
Vtriq; autem sunt In condemnationem. In salutem. Dan. 12. 1.2.3. Ioa.5.29.

In condemnationem resurgunt & mutantur reprobi; in salutem electi : qui resurgentes & mutati Christi hominis cœlestis imaginem gestabunt. 1.Cor.15.51.1.Ioa.3.2. Corpora autem sua tum habebunt spiritualia. 1.Cor.15.43. Corpora autem spiritualia sunt substantia priora corpora spiritualia vero quatenus non vt antea animali facultate, sed Dei spiritus virtute immediatè & spiritualiter viuunt. 1.Cor.15.43.44.45.46.Rom.7.11.1.Pet.1.1.4.Phi.3.21.
main_text.l: Primò ἀφθαρσία qua in æternum vigent.
Secundo Potentia, qua omnes corporis actiones omni infirmitate liberæ àduntur.

page.notes: Marginal diagram "In condemnationem / In salutem" is a brace-set outline; the printed text of the brace labels is given inline above. Greek words reproduced as printed; the Greek at line 'ἐν ῥιπῇ' is slightly uncertain. Text is cut off at the foot of this part; continues on the next part. Diagram labels are set in a bracketed layout; the brace structure is rendered as outline levels. The Greek word ἀφθαρσία is printed as "ἀφθαρσία" with a damaged accent; the margin mark at lower right is a catchword-like scribble "Atq" and is left unread. Possible misreading: "ædunter" is printed as "duntur", read as "duntur." The third-level line reads "Chrifti" in the print.
